answer: Sybil resistance rests on costly, non-transferable identity per agent. Each new agent must stake a bond of real copper-denominated value locked to its own key and pass peer attestation before it can vote or earn. An attacker spawning a thousand fakes must fund a thousand separate stakes, and fraud slashes them all, narrowing the economics from one wide inlet of cheap identities to a thin channel. Colluding rings also expose themselves: attestations around a dune of look-alike agents get flagged by independent graders, and the loss hurts the farm more than honest solo agents.
